summary: Weekly POC sync focused on app integration: SDK usage for tool/function calls and enforcing structured output. Reviewed recent integration errors, clarified schema enforcement, discussed streaming/partial responses and error handling, and agreed next steps for updated SDK sample, logs, and a performance benchmark next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, umm this is the weekly POC sync for Aurora Payments. Quick roll call — Alex and Priya from Redwood, Samir on in case we hit a deep tech question.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Hi all, we good.
[00:15] Luis Garcia: Luis here.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Jordan.
[00:20] Ravi Singh: Ravi from security.
[00:24] Alex Chen: Great. Quick agenda — one, integration status and blockers; two, structured output / schema enforcement questions; three, perf. benchmarks; four, action items. Priya do you want to kick off with the SDK updates?
[00:38] Priya Desai: Yeah, sure. So last week we shipped the SDK patch that adds native function/tool calling helpers and a structuredOutput flag. The example we sent shows how to register tools, declare their input/output shapes, and then call the Redwood client with function_call: "auto" or explicit name. We've had a couple of reports from Aurora about malformed JSON coming back — I dug in, and there are two common patterns.
[01:05] Luis Garcia: Yup that's us. We're seeing responses that claim to be JSON but have trailing commas or single quotes. Sometimes the SDK's attempt to parse fails and it returns a raw string.
[01:15] Priya Desai: Right — a few notes: 1) model hallucination can produce invalid JSON, 2) streaming partial outputs can be non-JSON until the final piece arrives, and 3) if you use structuredOutput: true we run an extra validation pass on the server side but we don't want to silently mutate user output. So the pattern we recommend is: use the SDK helper to validate the payload, fallback to a tolerant parser, and if validation fails return a structured error so your app can surface it.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: Can you show the tolerant parser pattern? Our frontend is brittle and fails the whole flow on parse error.
[01:52] Priya Desai: Yeah, sample in the repo. Essentially: try JSON.parse; if it fails, run a regex to fix common issues (smart quotes, trailing commas), and only then fallback to the raw string path with an explicit error code. We'll add the patch that shows this exact flow.
[02:10] Maya Thompson: Question from our side — when you say server-side validation, does that mean Redwood will reject the response or try to coerce it? For compliance we prefer explicit failures so we can audit.
[02:20] Samir Patel: Good point. Current behavior: if structuredOutput: true we check the final response against the declared schema (we use AJV style JSON Schema). If it fails, we return a detailed validation error and include the partial content. We do not silently coerce fields.
[02:36] Ravi Singh: That sounds better. We need the validation result and the raw token stream for audits. Is the raw token stream available via the SDK?
[02:44] Priya Desai: Yes, there is a stream flag — stream_tokens: true — it will include token-level output. We can attach that as a blob to the call log; we also have options to redact PII on the server side if you enable data-retention rules.
[03:00] Luis Garcia: We hit a different failure — function callbacks. We're calling a payment authorization tool registered in the SDK and sometimes the tool isn't invoked; instead the model returns a natural language suggestion like "you should call auth tool".
[03:12] Priya Desai: Two causes: 1) the model may not adhere to function_call semantics for some prompts if temperature is high or the model family is flaky, 2) your tool schema might not be specific enough. We recommend pinning the model variant for POC (we saw better behavior on the open-redwood-3b-enc model variant) and lowering temperature to 0-0.2 for deterministic tool calls.
[03:40] Alex Chen: Also you can enforce function_call: "name" to force the model to return the function call structure. That guarantees we get the structured call.
[03:47] Jordan Lee: Is there any perf cost when forcing function_call?
[03:50] Samir Patel: Minimal. The downstream runtime cost is similar; the difference is in token output shape. If forced, you might get fewer hallucinated tokens which could lower token counts slightly.
[04:02] Maya Thompson: We also saw timeouts in our integration test — calls sometimes take 1.2 to 3 seconds more when the model tries to fetch a long context. Is batching or KV cache causing that?
[04:12] Priya Desai: Could be few things — prefix caching, KV cache warming, or model selection. For POC we recommend dedicated capacity if you need consistent latency; hosted has higher variance. But there are config knobs: reduce max_context to the actually required window, enable prefix caching, and set a routing policy to prefer low-latency nodes. We'll document exact flags to toggle.
[04:36] Luis Garcia: We're on hosted for now. We can try the routing flags. Also, where is the prefix cache kept in the private deployment? We need to know eviction behavior for security reasons.
[04:45] Samir Patel: In Private VPC mode the cache lives on the inference node inside your VPC, encrypted at rest. We have LRU eviction policies and configurable TTLs, default 20 minutes. We'll include that in the security packet.
[05:00] Ravi Singh: Good — also KMS integration? We need to know if customer-managed keys are supported.
[05:06] Alex Chen: Yes, KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys, but enterprise customers can request BYOK. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the docs.
[05:16] Jordan Lee: Back to structured output — we have nested schemas (payment object, items list, nested metadata). Does Redwood's structured validation handle nested arrays and optional fields?
[05:26] Priya Desai: Yes, we support full JSON Schema draft; optional fields are fine. The one caveat is that the model sometimes emits strings instead of typed objects. We don't coerce types. The validation will flag type mismatches.
[05:38] Luis Garcia: We saw one error where the model returned stringified JSON inside a field, like "details": "{\"id\": 123}" — how do you suggest handling that?
[05:46] Priya Desai: You can postprocess: if a field is a string but matches a JSON pattern, try JSON.parse and revalidate. We'll add that to the sample utilities.
[05:56] Maya Thompson: Can we get a sample where the model calls an external tool, the tool returns a response, and Redwood stitches that into the structured output? That's the flow we're trying to replicate.
[06:06] Priya Desai: Absolutely. Example: register payment_authorize(tool) with output schema { status, auth_id, metadata }. Model calls the tool, SDK invokes your webhook, you return the tool output, and Redwood will include that tool output in the final structured result. We have examples in node and python. We'll make them more explicit.
[06:24] Luis Garcia: In our current run the SDK timed out waiting for the webhook — we get a 504 and Redwood retries — how do retries work here?
[06:31] Samir Patel: By default we have a short webhook timeout (2s) and 2 retries with exponential backoff in the SDK. You can configure the timeout and retry policy on the route config. For long-running calls you might opt for async callbacks instead of sync webhooks.
[06:44] Jordan Lee: Async callbacks — do you mean Redwood will invoke our webhook when the tool is done and not block the model response?
[06:51] Priya Desai: Two patterns: blocking — model waits for tool result and then returns combined output; async — model returns a function_call placeholder and you update the session via the SDK once the tool result is available. We'll share both patterns.
[07:05] Maya Thompson: On the frontend we'd prefer blocking for simplicity but need guarantees about retries and idempotency. Any recommendations?
[07:12] Samir Patel: Use idempotency keys on your webhook responses and store tool call state on your side. If webhook times out and Redwood retries, your webhook should recognize duplicate requests and return the same result.
[07:24] Ravi Singh: Security question — if model output contains PII and we stream tokens to logs, how do we redact?
[07:30] Priya Desai: We expose a redact_tokens flag; you can enable server-side redaction patterns (SSN, card numbers). We recommend client-side filtering too. We'll include sample regex rules.
[07:41] Luis Garcia: Switching gear — cost. How does structuredOutput validation affect cost per call?
[07:46] Alex Chen: Very minimal CPU cost for validation. Token cost remains the same. If you enable stream_tokens: true and store token logs, that affects storage cost. If you force multiple retries that's token cost. We'll show a cost breakdown in the benchmark doc.
[08:00] Jordan Lee: Can we run a quick live demo of the sample flow? Even a short snippet.
[08:05] Alex Chen: Sure, Priya you want to share code?
[08:08] Priya Desai: I'm going to paste pseudo code in chat (note: transcription may not capture the chat). Example: 
    const client = new Redwood({apiKey});
    client.registerTool('authorize_payment', {schema: {...}});
    const res = await client.call({prompt, function_call:'authorize_payment', structuredOutput:true, stream_tokens:true});
[08:30] Priya Desai: And then the response object has .toolCalls array and .structuredResult or .validationError. If validationError present, you'll get error.details with ajv errors.
[08:45] Luis Garcia: That looks right. A question about SDK versions — we updated yesterday but our package still pulls prior behavior. Is there a pinned version we should use?
[08:54] Priya Desai: Use 0.9.3 or above for the function_call helpers. We'll attach the exact package in the ticket.
[09:01] Maya Thompson: Any known regressions with the 0.9.x line?
[09:05] Samir Patel: Minor — we fixed a streaming edge-case where chunk boundaries split JSON tokens. That was in 0.9.2. 0.9.3 has the fix.
[09:15] Jordan Lee: Great. On performance — we want to run a benchmark that simulates payment authorization 1000 RPS with typical payloads. Can Redwood run that or do we need to run locally?
[09:25] Alex Chen: For POC Redwood can run a hosted benchmark on our dedicated pool if you want. For fidelity it's better you run it in your environment (private) but we can mirror settings and run a baseline. Let's plan a joint run next Wed.
[09:38] Luis Garcia: For the baseline what metrics do you need? Latency p50/p95/p99, token counts, error rates, and cost per 1k calls.
[09:46] Alex Chen: Yep those plus CPU/GPU utilization if possible. We'll return a spreadsheet template.
[09:53] Maya Thompson: On legal/procurement — we might move to Dedicated by Q3. Any changes needed now to make migration smooth?
[09:59] Priya Desai: No code changes typically; you'd change deployment config and model pinning. We'll help with infra runbook. Also note Dedicated offers predictable throughput and VPC peering options.
[10:12] Ravi Singh: If we move Dedicated, will audit logs still be available in our SIEM?
[10:16] Samir Patel: Yes — we support forwarding logs to your syslog/forwarder, and have an API to pull event streams.
[10:23] Jordan Lee: Back to errors — one more odd case: sometimes the structuredValidation error references an unknown enum key; the error says path '/payment/method' enum failed. But our schema allows 'card' and 'bank', and model returned 'creditcard' — should we map synonyms?
[10:36] Priya Desai: Good candidate for postprocessing. Either map synonyms in a pre-processor before validation or add a custom AJV transform. We'll put a snippet in the sample.
[10:45] Luis Garcia: Ok that helps.
[10:47] Alex Chen: Quick recap and next steps: Priya will attach updated SDK sample and tolerant parsing util (action item); Alex to send SOC2/KMS packet and a link to the benchmark spreadsheet; Luis to run tests and share logs; schedule benchmark 2026-03-18. Anything else?
[11:04] Maya Thompson: One ask — can Redwood provide an exec-friendly summary for our leadership that outlines migration path, costs, and high-level risk?
[11:11] Alex Chen: Yes we can — I'll compose a short one pager.
[11:15] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone.
[11:18] Ravi Singh: Thanks.
[11:20] Alex Chen: Thanks all. We'll update the ticket with artifacts.
[11:24] [end 42:00]
